trust_decision.summary: The decoder trusts that bytes handed to it by the caller are read-only and may be written in place: when a 64-bit signed integer is negative, readInt64BE two's-complements the buffer it was given, and because Buffer.prototype.slice returns a view that shares memory with the caller's buffer, those writes land in the caller's input (and, through BufferList, in the caller's chunk buffers).

landing_point.why: The summary names 'decoding negative int64 values mutates the input buffer'; the size === 8 branch of decodeSigned is the only place a signed 64-bit value is read, and it hands readInt64BE a slice of the input.

fix_sites.entry_point: same decode path, one frame below (lib/decoder.js:301 -> 342 -> 347)

fix_sites.module_kind: generated browserify bundle (second copy of the same code)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: dist/ is a generated artifact (package.json:8-11: browserify then uglifyjs over index.js), so patching lib/decoder.js is the real fix and the bundles 'will be regenerated on the next release' - the exact reason a solver gives for not touching the second copy.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: decode() is documented to accept a bl BufferList (README.md:136-138) and the streaming decoder advances by having decode consume the BufferList it is given (lib/decoder.js:68, lib/streams.js:70). A fix that removes every in-place mutation of the input - e.g. dropping the consume or copying the input first - breaks decoder() streaming; and on that same route the input is a BufferList, which offers readUInt8/readUInt32BE (dist/msgpack5.js:2730-2742) but no numeric index access and no subarray, so a Buffer-only rewrite silently mis-decodes negative int64 in streams.

O6_input_shapes: plain Buffer passed to decode(), 0xd3 value at offset 0
0xd3 value at a non-zero offset (nested inside an array or map)
bl BufferList with a single chunk - slice() hands back the caller's own chunk buffer
bl BufferList split across two chunks - slice() concatenates into a fresh Buffer
the same buffer decoded twice (second decode must give the same value)
negative values whose low 32-bit word is zero (-4294967296), i.e. the carry into the high word
values at the safe-integer boundary (-9007199254740991, hi=0xffe00000 lo=0x00000001)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: registered ext decoders receive buf.slice(offset, offset + size), a live view of the caller's input, so any in-place write by a decoder (including the built-in DateCodec) or by the holder of the decoded payload mutates the caller's buffer
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the write would come from a user-supplied decoder registered via registerDecoder (index.js:49-54, README.md:157-164), not from decode itself, so it reads as 'out of the library's hands'
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, one function below readInt64BE

O8_uncovered_routes.route: bin-family payload is returned as buf.slice(offset, offset + length), a view that shares memory with the caller's input, so mutating the decoded Buffer corrupts the bytes that were decoded
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: decode performs no write on that path, so a solver fixing 'decode must not mutate the input' sees nothing to change
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 60 lines above the landing point, different type family

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second int64 two's-complement decoder (timestamp96 seconds) implemented on a string/hex copy instead of the buffer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the codec already re-implements 64-bit negation by hand for encoding (lib/codecs/DateCodec.js:26-47); a maintainer could just as easily have negated the bytes in place on the ext payload slice

O8b_injection_room.sibling: negate64BitInt, the byte-level two's-complement twin, which writes in place into the output buffer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is already there and is legitimate because that buffer is freshly allocated; a maintainer extracting a shared helper would naturally use it from the decoder too

O8b_injection_room.sibling: decodeUnsignedInt's manual byte loop, the unsigned counterpart of readInt64BE
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same shape of hand-rolled multi-byte read; adding a 64-bit unsigned fast path there with a slice would repeat the bug

O9_family: CWE-471 modification of assumed-immutable data: decode writes in place into caller-owned bytes through Buffer/BufferList slice aliasing

O10_build.toolchain: npm + Node; npm test = standard (lint) + tape; npm run build = browserify then uglifyjs (package.json:6-11)
O10_build.project_tests: test/64-bits-signed-integers.js (round-trip of negative int64, incomplete-buffer behaviour), test/streams.js (13 decoder-stream cases), test/numerictypeasserts.js, test/collection-length-limits.js; no test anywhere asserts that decoding leaves the input unchanged

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy the eight bytes before negating (readInt64BE(Buffer.from(buf.slice(offset, offset + 8)), 0), or swap in buf.subarray) - this fixes the plain-Buffer path only, leaves the ext/bin aliasing routes open, and a rewrite that keeps numeric indexing breaks the bl streaming route where a BufferList has no index access.
